.claude/docs/workflow.md: Reference-based CLAUDE.md: a thin index (≤200 lines) with deeper content in `.claude/docs/` (on-demand) + `.claude/rules/` (path-scoped). `GENERATED:setup:*` is regenerated by setup-project; `USER:*` + `## Session Additions` are preserved across re-runs.

.claude/docs/stack.md: 1. Update `architecture.md` §Stack first → 2. update `Cargo.toml`/manifest → 3. re-run `/andromeda-setup-project` to refresh this file + rule version refs → 4. verify hooks/tooling → 5. commit `chore: bump {tool} to {version}`.

.claude/rules/frontend.md: - 2026-09-17: **In a webview spec, an expectation that interpolates the SAME expression on both sides of `.toBe()` cannot fail — and because `@wdio/globals`' `expect` has no message argument, the folding-context-into-the-value idiom makes that shape easy to write by accident.** Measured at `accessibility.e2e.ts`: `:384` compared `` `${names.length} reached [${names.join(' | ')}]` `` against `` `${focusableCount} reached [${names.join(' | ')}]` ``, and `:388` did the same with its `order:` half — the bracket lists were identical BY CONSTRUCTION, so "expected and received are identical to the character" was evidence of nothing, and half of `:388` asserted nothing at all. **The rule: the EXPECTED half must derive only from the DOM (or a literal), never from the value under test**; context may still ride along, but only as a term that cannot mask a difference. Verify by READING both halves — a vacuous assertion passes, so a green suite is not the check. **Corollary on IDENTITY:** key a reached/expected SET on element position within the live focusable set, never on the accessible NAME — two controls can share one (the coverage and report scroll regions are both unnamed `<div tabindex="0">`, each projecting to `DIV`, so a name-keyed `Set` silently collapses six elements into five, and the obvious `new Set(names).size` repair yields 5 against 6 and stays red). **Corollary on SENTINELS:** do not walk the Tab order waiting for a `BODY` stop — this webview's cycle need not contain one, and a sentinel walk then exhausts its cap and begins collecting from an arbitrary position; detect the lap by the first REPEATED element identity instead, which is wrap-invariant and fixed both Operable specs at once.

.claude/docs/commands.md: - `cargo modules generate tree` / `cargo tree` — module/dependency graph. `cargo public-api --simplified --workspace` — API surface.

.claude/rules/security.md: - 2026-10-11: A silent `cargo deny check licenses` is no evidence an allowed license still has a holder — `unused-allowed-license` defaults to warn — so count the holders (the `cargo metadata` license fields) before keeping or retiring an allow entry.

.claude/docs/design-summary.md: **Full plans:** `.andromeda/design-system.md` + `.andromeda/layout-templates.md`. Path-scoped rules `.claude/rules/frontend.md` + `a11y.md` are retirement stubs.

.claude/rules/testing.md: - 2026-10-12: **`tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` installs its OS handler on its first POLL, not on the call** — a test that spawns the listener and then raises SIGINT must `yield_now().await` once between them, or the signal meets the default disposition and kills the test process.
.claude/rules/verification-harness.md: - 2026-09-16: **A surviving grandchild holding an inherited stdout handle pins the parent after the child is dead — and `Start-Process -Wait` does not escape it** (it drains the redirection too). `$output = & cmd *>&1` holds the pipeline until every holder exits; measured as ~15 min of a CI step after the leg died, reproduced twice locally. Use `Start-Process … -PassThru` WITHOUT `-Wait`, then `$proc.WaitForExit()` — waits on the child alone (88 s on the same leg). A bare `*>` is not the alternative: PowerShell redirects write UTF-16/BOM that greps read as empty. Reap orphans yourself by START TIME, in REPEATED passes with a settle — the app tree outlives the child, so one enumeration at exit caught 7 of 27 where repeated passes took 17.

.claude/rules/observability.md: - 2026-06-26: Instrument a `#[tauri::command]` with a MANUAL `let _span = tracing::info_span!("tauri.command.<name>").entered();` at the top of the body — NOT the `#[tracing::instrument]` ATTRIBUTE. The attribute does not stack cleanly with `#[tauri::command]` (the command macro rewrites the fn signature for IPC arg-extraction, so instrument wraps the wrong shape). The manual span yields the same bounded `tauri.command.*` name (obs §4) and lets you log allowlisted fields (`count`, `latency_ms` — both already in the `conductor-core::redact` allowlist) on an `info!` boundary line. Errors returned to the webview go through `conductor_core::sanitize_error(&e)` (Display-not-Debug + host-path scrub), never the raw error. `conductor-tauri` gains a direct `tracing` dep for this (already a workspace dep — no new `Cargo.lock` package).
